#!/bin/bash
#FLUX --job-name=dr5-rep-tf
#FLUX --output=dr5-rep-tf_{{id}}.log
#FLUX --ntasks=1
#FLUX --cores-per-task=24
#FLUX --exclusive
#FLUX --no-requeue
#FLUX --time=23:00:00
#FLUX --gpus-per-task=2

# The SLURM --constraint=A100 option was not translated. Flux jobspec language can request resources
# with specific properties, but this is not exposed as a standard batch directive.
# This may affect job placement and prevent it from running on the intended hardware.
# For example, you may need to add `--requires=A100` to the `flux mini batch` command line.
# The SLURM --exclude option was not translated. Flux does not have a direct equivalent in its
# batch directives. This may result in the job running on an unintended node.

# Train Zoobot (tensorflow version) on DR5 shards from scratch on Slurm cluster.
# You will need to adjust various paths
# Run with flux mini batch replication/replicate.sh

pwd; hostname; date

nvidia-smi

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/share/apps/cudnn_8_1_0/cuda/lib64

ZOOBOT_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/zoobot
PYTHON=/share/nas2/walml/miniconda3/envs/zoobot/bin/python

# make these with shards_sbatch
# W+22a originally trained with validation data from an automatic subset of the train data,
# so there's no explictly-known validation set
TFRECORD_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/gz-decals-classifiers/data/decals/shards/all_2p5_unfiltered_n2
TRAIN_DIR=$TFRECORD_DIR/train_shards
TEST_DIR=$TFRECORD_DIR/eval_shards

THIS_DIR=/share/nas2/walml/repos/gz-decals-classifiers

EXPERIMENT_DIR=$THIS_DIR/results/tensorflow/dr5/efficientnet_dr5_tensorflow_greyscale

$PYTHON $ZOOBOT_DIR/zoobot/tensorflow/examples/train_model_on_shards.py \
    --experiment-dir $EXPERIMENT_DIR \
    --shard-img-size 300 \
    --resize-size 224 \
    --train-dir $TRAIN_DIR \
    --test-dir $TEST_DIR \
    --epochs 200 \
    --batch-size 512 \
    --gpus 2  \
    --wandb


# you might make (see shards.sh) and then train on some very small shards to debug everything first

# TRAIN_DIR=$ZOOBOT_DIR/data/decals/shards/decals_debug/train_shards
# EVAL_DIR=$ZOOBOT_DIR/data/decals/shards/decals_debug/eval_shards

# EXPERIMENT_DIR=$THIS_DIR/results/decals_debug

# python $ZOOBOT_DIR/train_model.py \
#     --experiment-dir $EXPERIMENT_DIR \
#     --shard-img-size 32 \
#     --resize-size 224 \
#     --train-dir $TRAIN_DIR \
#     --eval-dir $EVAL_DIR \
#     --epochs 2 \
#     --batch-size 8

issues: The script includes comments noting that the SLURM options '--constraint=A100' and '--exclude' were not translated. This is a critical omission, as the job may not be scheduled on the intended A100 GPU hardware, potentially leading to failed runs or incorrect performance benchmarks.

The Python application is launched with a '--gpus 2' flag. This is redundant given the '#FLUX --gpus-per-task=2' directive. While the values match, it is better practice for the application to rely on the scheduler-provided environment (e.g., CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) to determine GPU availability, reducing the risk of a mismatch.
The script hardcodes absolute paths for the Python interpreter and data directories. This makes the script brittle and not portable to other systems or user accounts.
The `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is managed manually. Using an environment module system (e.g., `module load`) is the recommended practice for managing software dependencies on HPC systems.

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=24
